# Offline Codex discovery fixtures

`schema/codex-cli-0.160.1/` contains unchanged files generated by the installed
`codex-cli 0.160.1` on 2026-10-30, with experimental methods included. The
neighboring provenance file records the command, individual SHA-256 hashes and
the aggregate schema hash. Generation writes local files only. No app-server,
proxy, socket, host, pairing or RPC was started or contacted.

Only `ProjectListResponse` (`project/list`) and
`RemoteControlStatusReadResponse` (`remoteControl/status/read`) are retained.
The adapter uses exact fields, required fields, nullability and enum/range
checks, plus bounded sizes, duplicate-key and unpaired-surrogate rejection. Its unknown-field
refusal is intentionally stricter than the generated draft-07 schemas.

The native project schema has `id`, `roots` and string-valued `metadata`; it has
no `projectKind`, `hostId` or repository identity. The status schema has
`installationId`, optional `environmentId`, `serverName` and connection status.
Neither native ID is substituted for the caller's provider host ID.

`responses/` contains synthetic response bodies shaped by those schemas, with
invented public fixture IDs and paths. These are result bodies, without JSON-RPC
envelopes. The caller supplies all pages in cursor order; a nonterminal last
cursor, duplicate project ID or malformed page cannot establish uniqueness.
Response-shape tests compare the Go decoder's fields/requiredness/nullability
with the generated schemas, and provenance tests verify their hashes.

`mac-chatgpt-only.json` is a separate **connector-evidence regression**, not an
app-server response or the original Mac payload. It reproduces exactly the
retained count and discriminants from #267 journal 2782: eleven entries with
`projectKind: chatgpt` and `hostId: null`. The journals did not retain their names,
IDs, roots or other wire fields. Nothing in this fixture invents Codex IDs.

Host/catalog binding, authorized source access and freshness, expected native
installation identity, and supported client pairing observations remain caller
responsibilities. The pure adapter checks the supplied binding but cannot
authenticate it. Daemon `connected` is insufficient pairing evidence;
`remoteControl/pairing/status` reports whether a supplied code was claimed and
is not used as a host-wide pairing assertion. Missing, mismatched or code-only
evidence remains `pairing_unknown`. Pairing-required evidence returns only the
verified managed-session owner action; it never generates a code or re-pairs.

Only normalized absolute POSIX roots are supported in this source slice. No
filesystem, symlink or Git inspection occurs. Thread creation, launch wiring,
handoff, links and runtime revalidation remain in 3/3b.
